purpose: Formalize (E≠0) as generation-by-exclusion: a candidate process-algebra operator that excludes perfect null closure and thereby generates admissible distinction.

formal_seed.interpretation: Applying exclusion stabilizes admissible distinction; reapplying the same exclusion does not create a stronger exclusion state.
formal_seed.null_rule: 0perfect is treated as an excluded operational limit, not as a realizable state.
formal_seed.non_arithmetic_rule: (E≠0) is not interpreted as a numeric inequality over ordinary energy.

allowed_uses: Distinguishing admissible non-null structure from perfect null closure.
Supporting local continuation conditions inside restricted topology domains.
Preparing formal relation to delta(E>0) through ⇔R.
forbidden_uses: Using ΠE as ordinary logical NOT.
Claiming proof that nothing cannot exist physically.
Treating E as ordinary conserved physical energy.
Using null unrealizability as a global metaphysical proof.

relation_to_core_expression.left_aspect_role: Generation of admissible distinction by exclusion of perfect null closure.
relation_to_core_expression.required_link: ΠE may only be coupled to continuation pressure through ⇔R under local, residue-preserving governance.
